text:
nina: Heads-up: after the release at 1744999000 we're seeing ~2-3x tail latency on the hosted runtime for long-context workloads (seq 1024+). Dashboard spike at 09:12 UTC.

devon: ugh. Any traces or flamegraphs? CI/bench showed green right?

nina: CI perf job failed on the release branch but merge proceeded because e2e was green. perf-bot posted the failure in #eng-runtime earlier: `perf/throughput long-seq regression +28%`

perf-bot: CI perf job: https://ci.redwood/perf/1234 - baseline=stable-2024-11, compare=release-2025-04, metric=latency_p99, delta=+28% :rotating_light:

mike_s: Can we bisect to the offending commit quickly? I can carve out some time for a git bisect + local perf run.

devon: I started a bisect on a repro harness (long-context bench). Quick notes: bad perf appears after merge of PR #4218 (kernel autotune tweaks). Candidate commit: a7c9e2f - "autotune: prefer quantized kernels for short warmup samples"

nina: that's the autotune change I flagged in review. It tried to be conservative but maybe the heuristic mis-evaluated sample distribution.

sam: paste the bisect output?

devon: bisect output:
```
$ git bisect start
# good: vstable
# bad: release-2025-04
# first bad commit: a7c9e2f autotune: prefer quantized kernels for short warmup samples
```
Also attached perf numbers from local runner:
- vstable p50/p95/p99: 12/28/62 ms
- release p50/p95/p99: 14/45/150 ms

mike_s: those p99s are huge. Any compile logs? Could be compile storm or fallback to slow kernels.

devon: yes - observed lots of "compiling kernel attention_v2, shape=(B, H, seq) seq=1024" spam in the logs during cold start (~1200 compile entries in 30s). Memory pressure triggered KV cache eviction frequently. Logs show: `kernel_autotuner: selected int8_attention_seq_optimized for layers 3-12` then immediate fallbacks: `kernel_loader: missing symbol for int8_attention -> compiling reference attention`

nina: that smells like a wrong autotune pick that isn't actually compatible with the compiled runtime (missing symbol) causing fallback to slow reference code. The autotuner probably picked a quantized kernel variant based on a small sample of short sequences.

sam: can we force the old kernel path as a mitigant? env? runtime flag?

mike_s: yes. Quick-hotfix: set KERNEL_AUTOTUNE_MODE=legacy or KERNEL_AUTOTUNE_OVERRIDE=fp16_compat in the runtime config. That prevents the new selection logic and avoids the compile storm.

devon: I pushed a staging deploy with KERNEL_AUTOTUNE_MODE=legacy and re-ran the long-seq bench. Results: p99 back to 65ms (close to stable). I also reproduced the compile storm locally with the autotune change applied.

ci-bot: perf regression guard: release-2025-04 failed threshold for metric latency_p99 on bench long-seq (job 1234). See https://ci.redwood/perf/1234.

nina: ok, plan: 1) revert the autotune heuristic commit (a7c9e2f) from release branch, 2) push config to prod to force legacy autotune as emergency, 3) add additional unit tests that exercise long-context sampling distribution and kernel selection logic. Agree?

mike_s: +1 for emergency config change and revert. I'll open the revert PR and request fast-track.

devon: also proposing we add telemetry counters for: autotune selection decisions (kernel id chosen, sample stats), compile failures, and fallback counts. We had two blind spots: no metric for compile storm and no label tying selection reason to sample distribution.

sam: nit: KV cache eviction looked correlated. When compile storm spiked, we saw many KV cache invalidations => worse latency. Might be because compiles kicked out resources and forced model reloads. Add a check to pin cache during compile?

mike_s: good catch. For immediate revert PR I've included a small change to ensure compile jobs run with lower OOM score and won't evict caches (runtime flag compile.priority=low-memory-impact).

nina: who will own the postmortem? We need to document root cause and follow-ups.

devon: I'll take the postmortem. Follow-ups: (a) revert commit rolled out and validated, (b) emergency config rollback removed after revert, (c) add autotune unit tests + telemetry, (d) add CI perf gate to block merge on long-seq p99 delta > 15% for release branches.

mike_s: Revert PR opened: https://git.redwood/reverts/458 - includes test and the compile.priority tweak. Requesting fast-track reviews from @nina and @devon.

sam: after staging smoke I can run canary on 10% of traffic to make sure no regressions.

nina: staging canary looked good after override. Production patching queued.

devon: marking this as rollout-blocker until revert merges and perf benchmark passes.

perf-bot: Canary perf run 1745002400 -> p99 delta vs stable = +3% (OK).

mike_s: thanks all. After revert merges I'll follow up with a small RFC for the autotune heuristics, and devon will own telemetry work.

nina: resolving for now but keeping thread pinned until postmortem complete. Action items: mike -> revert PR, devon -> postmortem + telemetry, sam -> canary run.

sam: ack.

devon: final note for postmortem: include suggested heuristic change: consider sequence-length histogram over full warmup window (not just N samples), and fall back to conservative kernels when compile toolchain symbols mismatch expected ABI.

mike_s: will also add a CI job that runs a short compile-storm detection harness on each autotune change PR.

nina: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
